interest: This document is particularly valuable for historians of World War II intelligence and economic warfare as it provides a comprehensive administrative record of Allied intercept operations directed against Japanese commercial radio traffic from wartime Chungking. It illuminates the inter-agency intelligence apparatus linking the State Department, the Office of War Information, the Board of Economic Warfare / Foreign Economic Administration, the Office of Naval Intelligence, and the Military Intelligence Division, including internal debates over whether the intercepted commercial traffic justified the effort of compilation. In addition, the file records early high-level Allied deliberations on the economic and political future of post-war Japan—such as State Department conferences with British scholar-diplomat Sir George Sansom and public inquiries regarding speeches by former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew—alongside strategic intelligence on oil demolitions in the Netherlands East Indies, resources in Hainan, and Japanese national income estimates.
overview: This file (894.50 File 131) is a three-page official Department of State 'List of Papers' (docket sheet / purport list) for decimal file 894.50, documenting incoming and outgoing communications and intelligence materials regarding Japanese internal economic affairs from July 1943 through June 1944 (sub-numbers 212 through 254). The bulk of the entries record regular diplomatic despatches from the U.S. Embassy in Chungking, under Ambassador Clarence E. Gauss and Chargé d'Affaires George Atcheson Jr., transmitting translations of intercepted Japanese commercial wireless messages monitored by the Office of War Information, the Office of Naval Intelligence, and Allied monitoring services. Other significant entries include economic warfare studies and reports from the Board of Economic Warfare and Foreign Economic Administration on Japan's war economy, occupation techniques, and the economic contribution of Hainan Island; memoranda of conversation concerning post-war Japan involving British diplomat Sir George Sansom; War Department reports on oil field demolitions in the Netherlands East Indies; public correspondence referencing speeches by former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew; and Moscow press reports on Japan's 1944 national income forwarded by Ambassador W. Averell Harriman.

subfiles.summary: This three-page administrative List of Papers (docket sheet) indexes communications, reports, and intercepted intelligence filed under Department of State decimal file 894.50 (Economic Affairs - Japan) from July 13, 1943, to June 19, 1944, covering sub-numbers 212 through 254. The predominant portion of the entries records regular despatches from the U.S. Embassy in Chungking forwarding translations of intercepted Japanese commercial radio messages gathered by the Office of War Information, Office of Naval Intelligence, and Allied monitoring posts. Other prominent entries include reports from the Board of Economic Warfare and Foreign Economic Administration regarding Japan's war economy and occupation techniques, records of discussions concerning post-war Japan with Sir George Sansom, reports on petroleum facility demolitions in the Netherlands East Indies, and Moscow press accounts of Japan's national income.
